thread:
Alice G.: Quick sync after the RFC: we need to nail probe ownership, decision latency, and the fallback candidate ordering before we enable auto-fallback for Dedicated. Two big questions: who owns probe tuning and who owns the fallback policy? Also, do we allow tenant-level probe overrides?

Ben K.: My take: runtime owns probe tuning (sample windows, smoothing, which signals to watch). Platform owns policy (what happens when probes trigger). Runtime knows signal fidelity; platform knows routing, quotas, and tiered fallbacks.

Cara M.: We can expose a tiny tenant-facing surface: sample_rate and sensitivity_hint. Defaults remain central. No per-tenant changes that alter fundamental routing semantics.

Dave S.: Oncall perspective: no free-for-all knobs. Hierarchy: central policy -> tenant hints. If tenants flip sensitivity wildly we get alert storms.

Fiona P.: Enterprise customers will ask for tenant overrides. Recommend locked-down override flow: request via support + audit + config-review.

Ben K.: Proposed decision edges for automatic fallback:
- transient spike -> soft-shift (move small % away)
- sustained failures past hard_threshold -> full degrade to fallback candidate
- telemetry anomaly (errors high, latency normal) -> route to degraded path but keep probing
These should be declarative in config-service.

Cara M.: State machine sketch (recon loop, not in-path):
```
STATES = {OK, SOFT_SHIFT, DEGRADED, EVICTED}
ON failure_event: incr(window_counter)
IF counter > soft_threshold -> SOFT_SHIFT (shift soft_pct)
IF counter > hard_threshold -> DEGRADED (route to candidate[0])
IF persistent && operator_ack -> EVICTED (drain)
```
Add hysteresis windows and cooldown to avoid flapping.

Alice G.: Metrics feeding counters: 5xx rate, p95 latency, cache-miss spike, OOM/recover events, and synthetic probe hits. Also track sample_count so we know signal confidence.

Dave S.: Observability: each variant emits a compact probe JSON: {status, p95_ms, errors_1m, sample_count}. Expose as a single signal endpoint for alerts.

Ben K.: Config schema example (stored in config-service):
```
{
  "variant":"redwood-v2",
  "soft_threshold":{"errors_per_min":"5","p95_ms":"1200"},
  "hard_threshold":{"errors_per_min":"20","p95_ms":"3000"},
  "soft_shift_pct":"10",
  "fallback_candidates":["fallback-small","fallback-int8","fallback-proxy"]
}
```
Platform ships defaults; tenant override via support. Candidates are ordered attempts.

Fiona P.: UX requirement: Console must show when fallback occurs, reason, which candidate is active, TTL of override, and how to run a rerun check. No silent degradations.

Cara M.: Implementation note: make decisions asynchronously. Decision service writes route intent; edge/router applies it. No in-path blocking. Add a TTL on intents so stale states expire.

Dave S.: Add operator abort endpoint + manual rollback. And require operator confirmation for evicting a variant.

Alice G.: Action list:
- Ben: PR for config schema + storage path in config-service
- Cara: prototype probe controller + reconciliation loop in runtime repo
- Dave: runbook stub + alert thresholds in oncall-docs
- Fiona: Console event UX + enterprise override workflow
Set sync Wed 10am next week.

Ben K.: One more Q: include quantization variants (int8) as part of fallback candidates or separate pathway?

Cara M.: Treat them as ordered candidates. Fallback list may include cheaper/quantized variants first, preserving IO contract. That lets us try lower-cost fallbacks before routing to a totally different service.

Ben K.: Good. Ensure compatibility checks on candidate list.

EmberBot: deploy-bot posted: "probe-controller v0.4 deployed to staging" :rocket:

Dave S.: I'll run canary tests simulating p95 spikes tomorrow to validate soft-shift and TTL expiry.

Fiona P.: Adding roadmap note so PMs can approve the override language for enterprise customers.

Alice G.: If anyone wants to contest ownership, call it out in the PR. Otherwise moving forward. :thumbsup:
